newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Chrysler to build Dakotas in Parana, Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to build Dakotas in Parana, Brazil.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Wednesday it would locate its new Dakota pickup truck assembly plant in Parana, a southern state of Brazil.
The U.S. No. 3 automaker announced last August it planned to invest $315 million into a facility that would build gasoline and diesel-powered Dakota trucks in Brazil.

Chrysler President Robert Lutz, who made the announcement at the Sao Paulo Auto Show, said in a statement the automaker chose Parana because of its transportation infrastructure, market access, skilled labor pool and quality of life.

The state is also geographically well-situated to serve the neighboring countries of Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, where Chrysler will export Brazilian-made Dakota trucks, Lutz said. Those countries, along with Brazil, are members of the Mercosur trade group.
Terms and details about the plant's location will be completed by the end of this year. Construction is expected to begin in early 1997.
Chrysler plans to build 12,000 units during the first year of production. Total annual capacity is expected to reach 40,000 units.

Separately, Detroit Diesel Corp said it would build a plant in Brazil to supply diesel engines for Dakotas and Jeep Cherokees produced at Chrysler's assembly plant in Cordoba, Argentina. The company has not decided on a site for that plant.
